symptom: The standalone trust-policy preflight validated the caller-owned envelope before examining policy anchors and proof references. An envelope own-descriptor Proxy could change a previously revoked witness anchor to ACTIVE, or repair a mismatching policy snapshot digest, before the later policy/reference reads. The standalone untrusted metadata-consistency flag could therefore describe a later claim rather than the claim present before envelope preflight; no independent authority or scoring was granted.
lesson: A standalone preflight is callable without the proof-request builder's detached snapshot. An earlier envelope validation may execute caller-controlled descriptor traps that change policy and proof-reference values before their subsequent validation. Strict shape checks alone cannot establish entry-time consistency.
guardrail: For standalone, deny-only policy/reference correlation, take bounded own-data-descriptor detached snapshots of policy and proof refs before traversing the envelope; then snapshot the envelope and perform all semantic checks on detached graphs only. Preserve invalid-envelope precedence, reject getters and exotic arrays, assert mutation triggers in two negative regressions, and never infer external trust or scoring.
